## What exists (read it before you plan)

- `ASupercutEnemy` is a plain `AActor` with a capsule (`SupercutEnemy.h`). `ASupercutGrunt::TickCombat`
  (`SupercutGrunt.cpp:63`) moves it with `SetActorLocation` inside a rectangle called its home: face the
  player, keep a distance band, sidestep on a clock, bounce off whatever it touches. No pathfinding, no
  gravity, no jumping. That is the robot he sees.
- Time: every enemy runs on its actor's own tick time. A freeze (the player's clapperboard) gives it a tick of
  zero seconds and everything stops where it is, mid-step and mid-windup (`SupercutEnemy.h`, the class
  comment). Whatever you build has to stop the same way: a Grunt frozen in the middle of a jump hangs in the

# Build farm for SUPERCUT

Lane farm1, 14 Nov 2026. Other PCs build, test, package and run SUPERCUT for lanes on c4. Git, agents and the
source of truth stay on c4. A farm PC holds a plain copy of a project folder (a "mirror"), never a git repo.

## Changes of 15 Nov 13:25 (main thread). These win over the older text below.

- **c4 is a farm host** (`farm.sh ... c4 ...`, root `D:\UE`, no ssh). `mirror c4 <name> <worktree>` copies nothing:
  it makes `D:\UE\Farm\<name>` a junction to the worktree, so steps build inside the worktree. Packages land in
  `D:\UE\Farm\_builds\<name>`, logs in `D:\UE\Farm\_out\<name>\<step>`. The owner freed c4 for this jam on 15 Nov
  ("C4 is free for lanes to use... speed is the priority"). No real input, no sound, and nothing in
  `D:\UE\Builds` or `D:\UE\Projects\Supercut59` is touched.
- **`farm.sh` queues by itself.** `build`, `test`, `package`, `package-shipping` and `run` take a slot in
  `D:\UE\Farm\_locks\<host>.<i>` (file `owner`: pid, name, step, start) and wait inside the call when none is free.
  Slots: [pc-c] 3, c4 2, [pc-b] 2, pc2 1. A `run` takes slot 1 only, so one game per PC at a time holds without
  anyone checking. A slot whose `farm.sh` is gone, or older than an hour, is freed by the next caller.
  `farm.sh slots` lists the holders. The load check in "Before a heavy step" is no longer needed for lanes; the
  rule about a tester's own `Supercut` process still is.

## SUPERCUT enemies lane (13 Nov 2026, c4, engine 5.9 preview)

All verified on c4 in the project at `D:\UE\Projects\Supercut59` on 13 Nov 2026.
Full report: `megajam-2026/lanes/enemies/HANDOFF.md`.

- **A unity build can break a file you did not touch** (verified, 13 Nov 2026). Unity builds paste
  several `.cpp` files into one, so their anonymous namespaces merge. `SupercutEnemy.cpp` had a
  function parameter `EyeHeight` and compiled. Adding two new `.cpp` files regrouped the unity blobs
  and put it next to `SupercutCharacter.cpp`, which has a file-local `const float EyeHeight`. The
  build then failed in the unchanged file: `C4459: declaration of 'EyeHeight' hides global
  declaration`. Fix: rename the parameter (`LookHeight`). Give file-local constants the class's
  prefix (`RusherEyeHeight`, `MarksmanLineColor`) so they cannot meet a twin in another file.
- **The `Pawn` collision profile ignores the `Visibility` channel** (verified, 13 Nov 2026). A sight
  check with `LineTraceTestByChannel(..., ECC_Visibility, ...)` passes through every body, which is
  right for "can it see the player". A line that must stop at the first body (the Marksman's aim
  line) needs `LineTraceSingleByObjectType` with `ECC_WorldStatic`, `ECC_WorldDynamic` and
  `ECC_Pawn`. The headless test `Supercut.Marksman.WalkingSidewaysThroughTheLockIsNotHit` checks
  that the line ends on the player.
- **Scripted runs: timers match from run to run, walked distances do not** (verified, 13 Nov 2026).
  The scripted player adds the controller's `DeltaTime` to its clock, and the world ticks with the
  same delta, so a step timed against an enemy's timer stays in step with it. To time a step, map
  the log's wall clock to the script clock through any `SCRIPT <t> ...` line, then read the enemy's
  log line on that clock. Every run of the three demos (seven in the editor, three packaged) landed
  each freeze in its planned window, some of them 0.1 s wide. But `CharacterMovement` integrates
  acceleration per frame, so how far a `move` step walks depends on the frame times. In the first

/**
 * What every enemy kind shares: health, taking a hit and its flash, dying, the one it fights, the
 * floor area it may move in, its number in the room, and stopping in a freeze.
 *
 * A kind (Grunt, Rusher, Marksman) is a wooden lay figure (AddFigure) that plays one clip at a time
 * (ShowClip), builds it in BuildBody and fights in TickCombat. Shots only ever meet the capsule.
 * Shots, upgrades, the run and the scripted player only ever see this class.
 *
 * A hit plays Hit_Chest, then the kind's own clip again. A killed enemy plays Death01 and lies where it
 * fell, holding the last frame, until the room goes. From the kill on, nothing of it collides.
 *
 * A hit while rolling also holds this enemy's own clock (USupercutTime::Hold, HitHoldSeconds, or
 * KillHoldSeconds on a kill, when Death01 waits for the hold to end) and shakes the drawn figure, never the
 * capsule or the actor (HitShakeCm). In a freeze neither happens.
 *
 * Everything runs on the actor's own tick time. The base joins the frozen scene, so a freeze gives
 * every kind a tick of zero seconds and the base returns before any kind code runs: mid-windup,
 * mid-lunge and mid-aim all stop where they are, and no timer counts. Its clip stops with it: the figure
 * ticks with the actor's time dilation.
 */
UCLASS(Abstract)
class ASupercutEnemy : public AActor
{
	GENERATED_BODY()

public:
	ASupercutEnemy();

	virtual void BeginPlay() override;
	virtual void Tick(float DeltaSeconds) override;

	void TakeHit(int32 Damage, const FVector& ShotDirection);

	int32 GetHealth() const { return Health; }
	bool IsDying() const { return bDying; }
	/** Enemies are numbered 0, 1, 2 in the order of their lines in the room file, whatever their kind. */
	int32 GetIndex() const { return Index; }
	FBox2D GetHome() const { return Home; }
	FVector GetChestLocation() const { return GetActorLocation() + FVector(0.f, 0.f, ChestHeight); }

	/** What its body is doing this frame (SupercutEnemyMotion.h). */
	const FSupercutEnemyMotion& GetMotion() const { return Motion; }

void ASupercutGrunt::Setup(int32 InIndex, const FBox2D& InHome)
{
	SetPlace(InIndex, InHome);
	// Stagger the first shots and the first sidestep so three Grunts do not act as one.
	FireClock = -0.45f * InIndex;
	StrafeClock = 0.7f * InIndex;
	StrafeSign = (InIndex % 2 == 0) ? 1.f : -1.f;
}

int32 ASupercutGrunt::GetStartHealth() const
{
	return FSupercutTuning::Get().GruntHealth;
}

void ASupercutGrunt::BuildBody()
{
	AddFigure(TEXT("Grunt"), GruntFigureScale);
	USceneComponent* Gun = SupercutEnemyGun::Add(this, GetFigure());
	MuzzleMaterial = SupercutShapes::Glow(this, SupercutShapes::SignalColor(SupercutShapes::ESignal::Danger), 1.f);
	// On the drawn muzzle. Its size is in world cm whatever the figure's scale.
	Muzzle = SupercutShapes::Add(this, Gun, ESupercutShape::Sphere, SupercutFigure::MuzzleOffset(false), FRotator::ZeroRotator, FVector(8.f), MuzzleMaterial);
	Muzzle->SetUsingAbsoluteScale(true);
	MuzzleHalo = SupercutShapes::AddHalo(this, Muzzle, ESupercutShape::Sphere, FVector::OneVector, SupercutShapes::SignalColor(SupercutShapes::ESignal::Danger));
	MuzzleHalo->SetScalarParameterValue(TEXT("Opacity"), 0.f);   // it comes in with the warning
}

FVector ASupercutGrunt::GetMuzzleLocation() const
{
	return Muzzle->GetComponentLocation();
}

void ASupercutGrunt::OnDying()
{
	Muzzle->SetVisibility(false, true);
}

// keylight pitch=-52 yaw=28 strength=4
// Read and checked, but it builds nothing: every room is lit by the desk lamp, which the room places from its own
// bounds (ASupercutRoom::BuildLight, the Light section of FSupercutTuning). Room files keep the line.
static FSupercutPieceType GKeyLightPiece(TEXT("keylight"), ESupercutPieceCount::AtMostOne, [](FSupercutPieceReader& In) -> FSupercutPieceBuild
{
	In.Number(TEXT("pitch"));
	In.Number(TEXT("yaw"));
	const float Strength = In.Number(TEXT("strength"));
	if (Strength <= 0.f)
	{
		In.Fail(TEXT("strength must be above 0"));
	}
	return [](ASupercutRoom&) {};
});

// grunt at=x,y,z facing=degrees home_from=x,y home_to=x,y
// A Grunt standing on the floor point at. It never leaves its home area, a rectangle on the floor.
static FSupercutPieceType GGruntPiece(TEXT("grunt"), ESupercutPieceCount::Any, [](FSupercutPieceReader& In) -> FSupercutPieceBuild
{
	const FVector At = In.Vector(TEXT("at"));
	const float Facing = In.Number(TEXT("facing"));
	const FBox2D Home = ASupercutEnemy::ReadHome(In, At);
	In.Note(TEXT("enemy"));
	return [=](ASupercutRoom& Room)
	{
		// The capsule is 92 cm tall from its centre; half a centimetre of air keeps its sweeps off the floor.
		const int32 Index = Room.TakeEnemyIndex();
		Room.SpawnPiece<ASupercutGrunt>(At + FVector(0.f, 0.f, 92.5f), FRotator(0.f, Facing, 0.f), [&](ASupercutGrunt& Grunt)
		{
			Grunt.Setup(Index, Home);
		});
	};
});

// blade at=x,y,z facing=degrees size=depth,length,thickness turns=1.5
// A bar that spins and kills on touch while it moves. at is its centre and facing is the way its axle points,
// which is the way the player walks past it. turns is full turns per second.
static FSupercutPieceType GBladePiece(TEXT("blade"), ESupercutPieceCount::Any, [](FSupercutPieceReader& In) -> FSupercutPieceBuild
{
	const FVector At = In.Vector(TEXT("at"));
	const float Facing = In.Number(TEXT("facing"));
	const FVector Size = In.Vector(TEXT("size"));
	const float Turns = In.Number(TEXT("turns"));
	if (Size.GetMin() <= 0.f || Turns <= 0.f)
	{
		In.Fail(TEXT("size and turns must be above 0"));
	}
	return [=](ASupercutRoom& Room)
	{
		Room.SpawnPiece<ASupercutBlade>(At, FRotator(0.f, Facing, 0.f), [&](ASupercutBlade& Blade) { Blade.Setup(Size, Turns); });
	};
});

/**

 *
 * The room does not know what pieces exist. Each line of the file belongs to a piece type
 * (SupercutRoomFile.h), and the piece type builds itself into the room with the functions in the
 * second half of this class. The room keeps what belongs to a room as a whole: its solid shapes
 * and lights, where the player starts, the end gate, the height below which a fall kills, and the
 * boxes that kill on touch. It also keeps a list of every actor a piece spawned, so that leaving
 * the room removes all of them.
 */
UCLASS()
class ASupercutRoom : public AActor
{
	GENERATED_BODY()

public:
	ASupercutRoom();

	int32 TearDown();

	virtual void Tick(float DeltaSeconds) override;

	// ---- What the run and the HUD read

	const FString& GetRoomName() const { return RoomName; }

	FVector GetHeroStart() const;
	float GetStartYaw() const { return StartYaw; }
	FVector GetGateLocation() const { return Gate; }
	float GetFallHeight() const { return FallHeight; }
	bool IsGateReached() const { return bGateReached; }
	/** The gate is locked while any enemy of this room is alive and not dying. A room with no enemies is open. */
	bool IsGateLocked() const { return bGateLocked; }
	/** How far the exit door at the gate stands open, degrees: 0 shut, about ExitDoorDegrees open. */
	float GetDoorAngle() const;
	/**
	 * Opens the gate if it is locked and no enemy of the room is left alive. The room asks every tick, and a kill asks

	 */
	void OpenGateIfClear();
	int32 CountPieceActors() const;
	/** What a fight leaves here: shot marks, landed chips, shells. It goes with the room. */

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- Grunt

IMPLEMENT_SIMPLE_AUTOMATION_TEST(FSupercutGruntTest, "Supercut.Grunt.FiresOnItsClockAndStopsWhenFrozen", SupercutTestFlags)
bool FSupercutGruntTest::RunTest(const FString& Parameters)
{
	FSupercutTestWorld World;
	if (!TestTrue(TEXT("test world starts"), World.Start()))
	{
		return false;
	}
	const FSupercutTuning& Tuning = FSupercutTuning::Get();
	ASupercutCharacter* Player = World.Spawn<ASupercutCharacter>(FVector::ZeroVector);
	ASupercutGrunt* Grunt = World.Spawn<ASupercutGrunt>(FVector(1000.f, 0.f, 0.f), FRotator(0.f, 180.f, 0.f));
	Grunt->SetTarget(Player);

	World.Run(Tuning.GruntFireInterval - 0.1f);
	TestEqual(TEXT("no shot before the first interval is up"), World.Count<ASupercutShot>(), 0);
	World.Run(0.2f);
	TestEqual(TEXT("one shot after 1.6 s"), World.Count<ASupercutShot>(), 1);

	// Freeze: the Grunt and its shot stop where they are, and its fire clock stops too.
	World.Time().PressClapper();
	ASupercutShot* Shot = *TActorIterator<ASupercutShot>(World.GetTestWorld());
	const FVector GruntHeld = Grunt->GetActorLocation();
	const FVector ShotHeld = Shot->GetActorLocation();
	World.Run(3.0f);
	TestTrue(TEXT("a frozen Grunt does not move"), Grunt->GetActorLocation() == GruntHeld);
	TestTrue(TEXT("its shot does not move"), Shot->GetActorLocation() == ShotHeld);
	TestEqual(TEXT("a frozen Grunt does not fire"), World.Count<ASupercutShot>(), 1);
	TestEqual(TEXT("the player is unhurt"), Player->GetHealth(), Tuning.PlayerHealth);

	// Resume: the shot lands, and the next one comes on the old clock.
	World.Time().PressClapper();
	World.Run(1.3f);
	TestEqual(TEXT("the slow shot lands for 20"), Player->GetHealth(), Tuning.PlayerHealth - Tuning.GruntShotDamage);
	return true;
}

	// And the other way: a template written from other values, read over the defaults, gives those values.
	// Each other value is inside the field's range, on a step of 1/8 (exact in a float), and not its default.
	FSupercutTuning Other;
	for (const FEntry& Entry : TuningFile::Entries())
	{
		if (Entry.Kind == EKind::Section)
		{
			continue;
		}
		bool bFound = false;
		for (const double Share : { 0.5, 0.25, 0.75, 0.4 })
		{
			const double Value = Entry.Kind == EKind::Float ? FMath::RoundToDouble((Entry.Lowest + Share * (Entry.Highest - Entry.Lowest)) * 8.0) / 8.0
				: FMath::RoundToDouble(Entry.Lowest + Share * (Entry.Highest - Entry.Lowest));
			const double Default = Entry.Kind == EKind::Float ? double(Defaults.*Entry.FloatField) : double(Defaults.*Entry.WholeField);
			if (Value >= Entry.Lowest && Value <= Entry.Highest && Value != Default)
			{
				if (Entry.Kind == EKind::Float)
				{
					Other.*Entry.FloatField = float(Value);
				}
				else
				{
					Other.*Entry.WholeField = int32(Value);
				}
				bFound = true;
				break;
			}
		}
		TestTrue(FString::Printf(TEXT("%s has another value inside its range"), Entry.Name), bFound);
	}
	FSupercutTuning Read;
	const FReadResult FromOther = TuningFile::Parse(TuningLines(TuningFile::WriteTemplate(Other)), Read);
	TestEqual(TEXT("the other template has no bad line"), FromOther.Problems.Num(), 0);
	TestTrue(TEXT("reading it gives the other values byte for byte"), FMemory::Memcmp(&Read, &Other, sizeof(Other)) == 0);
	TestEqual(TEXT("every field differs from its default"), TuningFile::ChangedNames(Read).Num(), TuningFieldCount());
	return true;

/**
 * The one owner of time: rolling or frozen, the clapperboard charges and the freeze timer.
 *
 * How a freeze works: every actor that belongs to the scene (enemies, their shots, machines) calls
 * JoinScene once. While frozen, each of them has AActor::CustomTimeDilation set to 0. The engine
 * multiplies an actor's tick time, and its components' tick time, by that number, so a frozen actor
 * still ticks but with zero seconds passed. It does not move, its timers do not count, and nothing
 * about it is lost. The player, the gun and the HUD never join, so they run on.
 */
UCLASS()
class USupercutTime : public UTickableWorldSubsystem
{
	GENERATED_BODY()

public:
	/** The time system of the world this object lives in. Fails loudly if there is none. */
	static USupercutTime& Get(const UObject* WorldContext);

	virtual void Initialize(FSubsystemCollectionBase& Collection) override;
	virtual void Tick(float DeltaTime) override;
	virtual TStatId GetStatId() const override;

	/** The clapperboard. Rolling: spends a charge and freezes. Frozen: ends the freeze early. Returns false when nothing happened (no charges). */
	bool PressClapper();

	bool IsFrozen() const { return bFrozen; }
	int32 GetCharges() const { return Charges; }
	int32 GetMaxCharges() const { return MaxCharges; }
	float GetFreezeLength() const { return FreezeLength; }

	/** How long a freeze lasts and how many charges a full board holds. The run sets these from the tuning and the upgrades held. */
	void SetRules(float InFreezeLength, int32 InMaxCharges);

	/** A new room: the board is full again. */
	void RefillCharges();

	/** One charge back, up to the most the board holds. Returns false when the board was full already. */
	bool AddCharge();

	/** Seconds of real time since a charge was last gained. For the HUD. */
	float GetSecondsSinceChargeGained() const { return SinceChargeGained; }

	/**
	 * The room is over: ends a freeze that is still on and forgets every scene actor.
	 * The run calls this just before it destroys them.
	 */
	void EndScene();

	/** How many live actors are in the scene list. */
	int32 CountSceneActors() const;
	float GetFreezeRemaining() const { return bFrozen ? Remaining : 0.f; }

	/** Seconds of real time since the state last changed. For pictures and animation. */
	float GetSecondsSinceChange() const { return SinceChange; }

		bAwake = true;
		UnseenClock = 0.f;
	}
	else
	{
		UnseenClock += DeltaSeconds;
	}

	const float WindupStart = Tuning.GruntFireInterval - Tuning.GruntWindup;
	const float ClockBefore = FireClock;

## For the enemy AI lane

Read from branch gen3 at `D:\UE\wt\gen3` (15 Nov 16:45). All lengths cm, z up, the floor a player starts on at z 0.
Rooms are text files (`Content/Rooms/gen/sN/dNN.txt`), one piece per line, built by ASupercutRoom
(Source/Supercut/SupercutRoom.cpp) and the piece types in SupercutRoomPieces.cpp and SupercutPuzzles.cpp.

**What a room is made of.** Every solid surface is a `box` line: one axis-aligned UStaticMeshComponent on the room
actor, collision profile `BlockAll` (ASupercutRoom::AddBox / AddShape, SupercutRoom.cpp:282). There are no separate
actors per box and no tags. The role word (`role=floor|wall|ledge|crate|flat|scorch|metal`) only picks the material;
the room keeps no per-box role you can query at run time. `mark` and `prop` lines and the tape crosses are `NoCollision`
(walk-through, look only). Catalogue set dressing (`dress` lines) is solid only when its catalogue entry says
`blocks=1`; open dressing has no collision.

**A fire pit.** A real hole in the floor, not a flat danger strip:
- the floor boxes round the opening are cut (sc_build.py `carve_pits`), so the opening has no floor collision;
- a 20 cm burnt lip runs round the opening at floor level: `box role=scorch`, 20 thick, from z -160 to 0. Its top is
  walkable floor, flush with the floor;
- the bed: `box role=scorch` from z -180 to -160 (solid);
- the glow on the bed: `mark role=lava` (no collision);
- the hazard: `kill from=... to=... cause=lava`, the opening only (not the lip), from the bed (z -160) to z +5.
  A kill box is not a component or actor and has no collision channel. It is a box in ASupercutRoom::KillBoxes,
  asked through `ASupercutRoom::TouchesKillBox(At, Radius, HalfHeight)` (SupercutRoom.h:109). Enemies already use it:
  `ASupercutEnemy::WouldTouchKillBox` (SupercutEnemy.cpp:175) keeps Grunts and Rushers from stepping in. That call is
  the way to tell hazard from floor: a point over an opening touches a kill box, a point on floor or lip does not.
- cause word `lava` is every fire in generated rooms (fire pits and lava hops). Blades kill by actor, not kill box.
- `fall below=Z` (one per room, 350 under the room's lowest floor) kills only the player; nothing catches an enemy
  that drops into a pit. A pit is 160 deep with sheer walls: an enemy that falls in cannot climb out.

namespace
{
	const float ShoveTestStep = 0.01f;   // seconds per tick
	const float ShoveTestSettle = 0.5f;  // long enough for any hold and slide to be over

	/** A game world playing tests/shove: a wall at x 1500 to 1560 (y -400 to 400), lava at x 1500 to 1700 (y 800 to
	 *  1200), and one Grunt whose home area ends at x 1010. */
	struct FShoveTestWorld : FTestWorldWrapper
	{
		bool Start()
		{
			if (!CreateTestWorld(EWorldType::Game))
			{
				return false;
			}
			GetTestWorld()->GetWorldSettings()->DefaultGameMode = AGameModeBase::StaticClass();
			if (!BeginPlayInTestWorld())
			{
				return false;
			}
			Runner().Begin({ TEXT("tests/shove") }, 1);
			for (TActorIterator<ASupercutGrunt> It(GetTestWorld()); It; ++It)
			{
				It->bPassive = true;   // the room's own Grunt stands still and never shoots
			}
			return Runner().GetHero() && Runner().GetRoom();
		}

		void Run(float Seconds)
		{
			const int32 Ticks = FMath::RoundToInt(Seconds / ShoveTestStep);
			for (int32 Tick = 0; Tick < Ticks; ++Tick)
			{
				TickTestWorld(ShoveTestStep);
			}
		}

		USupercutRun& Runner() { return USupercutRun::Get(GetTestWorld()); }
		USupercutTime& Time() { return USupercutTime::Get(GetTestWorld()); }

		/** A passive Grunt on the floor at X, Y with no home area. It joins the scene as it starts. */
		ASupercutGrunt* Stand(float X, float Y)
		{
			FActorSpawnParameters Params;
			Params.SpawnCollisionHandlingOverride = ESpawnActorCollisionHandlingMethod::AlwaysSpawn;
			ASupercutGrunt* Grunt = GetTestWorld()->SpawnActor<ASupercutGrunt>(FVector(X, Y, 0.f), FRotator::ZeroRotator, Params);
			Grunt->bPassive = true;
			Grunt->SetActorLocation(FVector(X, Y, HalfHeight(Grunt)));
			return Grunt;
		}

		static float Radius(const ASupercutGrunt* Grunt) { return CastChecked<UCapsuleComponent>(Grunt->GetRootComponent())->GetScaledCapsuleRadius(); }
		static float HalfHeight(const ASupercutGrunt* Grunt) { return CastChecked<UCapsuleComponent>(Grunt->GetRootComponent())->GetScaledCapsuleHalfHeight(); }
	};

	struct FShoveTuningRestore
	{
		~FShoveTuningRestore() { FSupercutTuning::Get() = FSupercutTuning(); }
	};

	const EAutomationTestFlags ShoveTestFlags = EAutomationTestFlags_ApplicationContextMask | EAutomationTestFlags::ProductFilter;
	const FVector ShoveTestAlongX(1.f, 0.f, 0.f);
}

		if (Step.Command == TEXT("scene"))

			if (Run.GetRoomEntries() == RoomEntriesSeen)
			{
				// Still in the old room, or on a screen between rooms. Wait here.
				SceneWait += DeltaTime;
				if (SceneWait > SceneWaitLimit)
				{
					FailScript(FString::Printf(TEXT("waited %.0f s at a \"scene\" line and the run did not enter a new room"), SceneWaitLimit));

#!/bin/bash
# farm.sh: build, test, package and run a SUPERCUT project copy on a farm PC, driven from c4. Details: ../FARM.md.
#
#   farm.sh mirror  <host> <name> <project folder on c4>     copy the project to <root>\Farm\<name> (changed files only)
#   farm.sh build   <host> <name> <log folder> [build.ps1 args, e.g. -Target Supercut -Jobs 8]
#   farm.sh test    <host> <name> <log folder> [run_tests.ps1 args, e.g. -Filter Supercut.Rooms]
#   farm.sh package <host> <name> <log folder>               Tools\package.cmd   -> <root>\Farm\_builds\<name>\Supercut59
#   farm.sh package-shipping <host> <name> <log folder>      Tools\package_shipping.cmd -> ...\_builds\<name>\Supercut59_ship
#   farm.sh run     <host> <name> <log folder> [run_demo.ps1 args]   {P} = the mirror folder there, e.g. -Script {P}\Script\main8.txt
#   farm.sh fetch   <host> <name> <remote path> <local folder>   path in the mirror, or builds/... or out/...
#   farm.sh status  <host>
#   farm.sh slots                                             who holds or waits for which PC right now
#
# Each step brings its logs back to <log folder>/<step>/ and exits with the remote step's exit code.
# Logs that come back have the PC's user and computer names replaced by USER and PC.
#
# Hosts: [pc-b], pc2, [pc-c], pc4 over ssh, and c4 itself (15 Nov: the owner freed c4 for lanes). On c4 nothing is
# copied: "mirror" makes D:\UE\Farm\<name> a junction to the project folder, so the steps build in that folder.
#
# Slots (15 Nov): build, test, package, package-shipping and run take one of the host's slots and wait for one
# when all are taken, so the lanes no longer pile onto one PC. A slot whose farm.sh has died is taken over.
set -u
here=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
root_of() {   # one line per farm PC: ssh alias, root folder there (engine in <root>\UE_5.9, mirrors in <root>\Farm)
  case "$1" in
    [pc-b]) echo 'C:\UE' ;;
    pc2)    echo 'C:\UE' ;;
    [pc-c])   echo 'F:\UE' ;;
    pc4)    echo 'C:\UE' ;;
    c4)     echo 'D:\UE' ;;
    *) echo "FARM unknown host '$1' ([pc-b], pc2, [pc-c], pc4, c4)" >&2; exit 64 ;;
  esac
}
slots_of() {  # heavy steps at once on each PC
  case "$1" in
    [pc-b]) echo 2 ;;
    pc2)    echo 1 ;;
    [pc-c])   echo 3 ;;
    c4)     echo 2 ;;
    *)      echo 1 ;;
  esac
}
fwd() { echo "${1//\\//}"; }   # C:\UE -> C:/UE for scp and tar
is_local() { [ "$1" = c4 ]; }
lockdir=/d/UE/Farm/_locks
slot=''
ubt=''
# UnrealBuildTool runs one at a time per engine copy, and a package that meet

	FActorSpawnParameters Params;
	Params.SpawnCollisionHandlingOverride = ESpawnActorCollisionHandlingMethod::AlwaysSpawn;

	check(Effect);
	Effect->Kind = Kind;
	Effect->Life = Life;
	Effect->Particles->SetAsset(Systems[int32(Kind)]);
	return Effect;

void USupercutEffects::EnemyHit(const FVector& At, const FVector& ShotDirection, bool bKill)
{
	const FSupercutTuning& Tuning = FSupercutTuning::Get();
	const float Size = bKill ? Tuning.KillBurstSize : Tuning.HitBurstSize;
	if (Size <= 0.f)
	{
		return;
	}
	// Back out of the hit, toward the shooter, like the chips, so the figure does not hide the burst.
	const FVector Out = -ShotDirection.GetSafeNormal(UE_SMALL_NUMBER, FVector::ForwardVector);
	ASupercutEffect* Effect = Spawn(ESupercutEffect::WoodBurst, At, Out.Rotation(), VfxBurstSeconds + VfxSpareSeconds);
	Effect->Particles->SetVariableFloat(TEXT("Size"), Size);
	Effect->Particles->Activate(true);
	USupercutTime::Get(this).JoinScene(Effect);
}

void USupercutTime::JoinScene(AActor* Actor)
{
	check(Actor);
	SceneActors.AddUnique(Actor);
	Actor->CustomTimeDilation = DilationFor(Actor);
	if (bFrozen)
	{
		HeldAt.Add(Actor, Actor->GetActorTransform());
	}
}

void USupercutTime::Hold(AActor* Actor, float Seconds)
{
	check(Actor);
	checkf(SceneActors.Contains(Actor), TEXT("USupercutTime::Hold: %s is not in the scene"), *Actor->GetName());
	if (bFrozen || Seconds <= 0.f)
	{
		return;
	}
	FHold& Held = Holds.FindOrAdd(Actor);
	Held.Remaining = FMath::Max(Held.Remaining, Seconds);
	Held.SetFrame = GFrameCounter;
	Actor->CustomTimeDilation = DilationFor(Actor);
	UE_LOG(LogSupercut, Display, TEXT("FEEL hold start %s %.3f s"), *Actor->GetName(), Seconds);
}

void USupercutTime::SetFrozen(bool bNewFrozen, const TCHAR* Why)
{
	const float Length = FreezeLength;
	const float Held = Length - Remaining;

	bFrozen = bNewFrozen;
	SinceChange = 0.f;

	int32 Count = 0;
	for (int32 Index = SceneActors.Num() - 1; Index >= 0; --Index)

	}

bool ASupercutEnemy::CanSee(const AActor* TargetActor, float Range, float LookHeight) const
{
	const FVector Here = GetActorLocation();
	const FVector There = TargetActor->GetActorLocation();
	if (FVector::Dist2D(Here, There) > Range)
	{
		return false;
	}
	FCollisionQueryParams Params(SCENE_QUERY_STAT(SupercutEnemySight), false, this);
	Params.AddIgnoredActor(TargetActor);
	return !GetWorld()->LineTraceTestByChannel(Here + FVector(0.f, 0.f, LookHeight), There + FVector(0.f, 0.f, 30.f), ECC_Visibility, Params);
}

void USupercutEffects::ShotImpact(const FHitResult& Hit)
{
	const FSupercutTuning& Tuning = FSupercutTuning::Get();
	const AActor* Other = Hit.GetActor();
	if (Tuning.ImpactEffectSize <= 0.f || !Other || Other->IsA<ASupercutEnemy>() || Other->IsA<ASupercutCharacter>())
	{
		return;
	}
	const ESupercutSurface Surface = SurfaceOf(Hit);
	const FVector Out = Hit.ImpactNormal.GetSafeNormal(UE_SMALL_NUMBER, FVector::UpVector);
	ASupercutEffect* Effect = Spawn(Surface == ESupercutSurface::Metal ? ESupercutEffect::ImpactSparks : ESupercutEffect::ImpactDust, Hit.ImpactPoint + Out, Out.Rotation(), VfxImpactSeconds + VfxSpareSeconds);
	Effect->Particles->SetVariableFloat(TEXT("Size"), Tuning.ImpactEffectSize);
	if (Surface != ESupercutSurface::Metal)
	{
		const FVfxDustCounts& Counts = Surface == ESupercutSurface::Wood ? VfxWoodCounts : VfxHardCounts;
		Effect->Particles->SetVariableInt(TEXT("SparkCount"), Counts.Sparks);
		Effect->Particles->SetVariableInt(TEXT("GritCount"), Counts.Grit);
		Effect->Particles->SetVariableInt(TEXT("SplinterCount"), Counts.Splinters);
		Effect->Particles->SetVariableInt(TEXT("WoodDustCount"), Counts.WoodDust);
		Effect->Particles->SetVariableInt(TEXT("PlasterDustCount"), Counts.PlasterDust);
	}
	Effect->Particles->Activate(true);
	// A short warm light on the surface round the hit, gone in three frames.
	UPointLightComponent* Light = NewObject<UPointLightComponent>(Effect);
	Light->SetupAttachment(Effect->GetRootComponent());
	Light->SetRelativeLocation(FVector(VfxImpactLightOut - 1.f, 0.f, 0.f));   // the effect sits 1 cm off the surface, X along the normal
	Light->SetMobility(EComponentMobility::Movable);
	Light->SetIntensityUnits(ELightUnits::Candelas);
	Light->SetIntensity(VfxImpactLightCandelas);
	Light->SetLightColor(VfxLightColour);
	Light->SetAttenuationRadius(VfxImpactLightReach);
	Light->SetCastShadows(false);
	Light->RegisterComponent();
	Effect->Light = Light;
	Effect->LightSeconds = VfxImpactLightSeconds;
	Effect->LightStrength = VfxImpactLightCandelas;
	USupercutTime::Get(this).JoinScene(Effect);
}

ESupercutSurface USupercutEffects::SurfaceOf(const FHitResult& Hit)
{
	UPrimitiveComponent* Part = Hit.GetComponent();

{

const FSupercutWalkGrid* USupercutNav::GetGrid()
{
	ASupercutRoom* Room = USupercutRun::Get(this).GetRoom();
	if (!Room)
	{
		return nullptr;
	}
	if (BuiltFor.Get() == Room && Grid.IsValid())
	{
		return Grid.Get();
	}

	// The room's solid parts, as the hall measures them (SupercutHall.cpp).
	const FSupercutTuning& Tuning = FSupercutTuning::Get();
	FSupercutWalkGrid::FSettings Settings;
	TInlineComponentArray<UPrimitiveComponent*> Parts(Room);
	for (const UPrimitiveComponent* Part : Parts)
	{
		if (Part->IsCollisionEnabled())
		{
			Settings.Bounds += Part->Bounds.GetBox();
		}
	}
	checkf(Settings.Bounds.IsValid, TEXT("USupercutNav: room %s has no solid parts"), *Room->GetRoomName());
	Settings.CellSize = Tuning.GruntCellSize;
	Settings.StepHeight = Tuning.GruntStepHeight;
	Settings.LowestFloor = Room->GetFallHeight();
	Grid = MakeShared<FSupercutWalkGrid>();
	Grid->Build(GetWorld(), Settings, [&](const FVector& Centre) { return Room->TouchesKillBox(Centre, Settings.Radius, Settings.HalfHeight); });
	BuiltFor = Room;
	++Builds;
	UE_LOG(LogSupercut, Display, TEXT("NAV room %s grid %d x %d, walk %d, edge %d, blocked %d, hazard %d"), *Room->GetRoomName(), Grid->GetSizeX(), Grid->GetSizeY(),
		Grid->CountCells(FSupercutWalkGrid::ECell::Walk), Grid->CountCells(FSupercutWalkGrid::ECell::Edge), Grid->CountCells(FSupercutWalkGrid::ECell::Blocked),
		Grid->CountCells(FSupercutWalkGrid::ECell::Hazard));
	return Grid.Get();
}

bool FSupercutGruntAIFreezeTest::RunTest(const FString& Parameters)
{
	FGruntAITuningRestore Restore;
	FSupercutTuning::Get().PlayerHealth = 1.0e9f;
	FGruntAIWorld World;
	if (!TestTrue(TEXT("test world starts in tests/gruntai_wall"), World.Start(TEXT("tests/gruntai_wall"))))
	{
		return false;
	}
	// The Grunt sees the player, then the player goes behind the wall: it walks round to see them.
	World.PutHero(FVector(2000.f, 600.f, 0.f));
	World.Run(1.f);
	World.PutHero(FVector(1200.f, 600.f, 0.f));
	ASupercutGrunt* Grunt = World.Grunts()[0];
	float Waited = 0.f;
	while (Waited < 20.f && Grunt->GetMotion().Velocity.Size2D() < 150.f)
	{
		World.Run(GruntAITestStep);
		Waited += GruntAITestStep;
	}
	if (!TestTrue(TEXT("the Grunt walks within 20 s"), Waited < 20.f))

	const FVector Held = Grunt->GetActorLocation();
	const FRotator Facing = Grunt->GetActorRotation();
	const FVector Velocity = Grunt->GetMotion().Velocity;

	TestEqual(TEXT("frozen, it does not move"), Grunt->GetActorLocation(), Held);
	TestEqual(TEXT("frozen, it does not turn"), Grunt->GetActorRotation(), Facing);
	TestEqual(TEXT("frozen, its Motion keeps its velocity"), Grunt->GetMotion().Velocity, Velocity);
	World.Time().PressClapper();
	World.Run(0.2f);
	TestTrue(TEXT("rolling again, it walks on"), FVector::Dist2D(Grunt->GetActorLocation(), Held) > 10.f);
	return true;
}

`StepLeft` starts at 0, so a Grunt standing still would play a step on its first tick. Fixing that, and reading the duck state directly instead of last frame's `Motion`.

**Sun 15 Nov 17:39:54 · Tool call: Bash** (Play steps only when it moved)

```

o='''		StepLeft -= FVector::Dist2D(Before, GetActorLocation());
		if (StepLeft <= 0.f)
		{
			USupercutAudio::Get(this).PlayAt(TEXT("grunt_step"), GetActorLocation() - FVector(0.f, 0.f, Capsule->GetUnscaledCapsuleHalfHeight()));
			StepLeft += Motion.bCrouched ? Tuning.GruntCrouchStepCm : Tuning.GruntStepCm;
		}
'''
n='''		const float Walked = FVector::Dist2D(Before, GetActorLocation());
		StepLeft -= Walked;
		if (Walked > 0.f && StepLeft <= 0.f)
		{
			USupercutAudio::Get(this).PlayAt(TEXT("grunt_step"), GetActorLocation() - FVector(0.f, 0.f, Capsule->GetUnscaledCapsuleHalfHeight()));
			StepLeft += Crouched >= 0.5f ? Tuning.GruntCrouchStepCm : Tuning.GruntStepCm;

'''

open(p,'wb').write(b.replace('\n','\r\n').encode('utf-8'))

IMPLEMENT_SIMPLE_AUTOMATION_TEST(FSupercutGruntAIStepTest, "Supercut.GruntAI.AWalkingGruntStepsByTheGroundItCovers", GruntAITestFlags)
bool FSupercutGruntAIStepTest::RunTest(const FString& Parameters)
{
	FGruntAITuningRestore Restore;
	FSupercutTuning& Tuning = FSupercutTuning::Get();
	Tuning.PlayerHealth = 1.0e9f;
	FGruntAIWorld World;
	if (!TestTrue(TEXT("test world starts in tests/gruntai_wall"), World.Start(TEXT("tests/gruntai_wall"))))
	{
		return false;
	}
	const USupercutAudio& Audio = USupercutAudio::Get(World.GetTestWorld());
	auto CountSteps = [&Audio](int32 From)
	{
		int32 Steps = 0;
		for (int32 Each = From; Each < Audio.GetAsked().Num(); ++Each)
		{
			Steps += Audio.GetAsked()[Each].StartsWith(TEXT("grunt_step")) ? 1 : 0;
		}
		return Steps;
	};
	// Seen, then hidden behind the wall: it walks round the wall's end, a long walk with stops to fire.
	ASupercutGrunt* Grunt = World.Grunts()[0];
	const int32 Start = Audio.GetAsked().Num();
	World.Run(1.f);
	TestEqual(TEXT("asleep and standing, it makes no steps"), CountSteps(Start), 0);
	World.PutHero(FVector(2000.f, 600.f, 0.f));
	World.Run(1.f);
	World.PutHero(FVector(1200.f, 600.f, 0.f));
	const int32 Mark = Audio.GetAsked().Num();
	float Walked = 0.f;
	for (int32 Tick = 0; Tick < 6 * 60; ++Tick)
	{
		const FVector Before = Grunt->GetActorLocation();
		World.Run(GruntAITestStep);
		Walked += FVector::Dist2D(Before, Grunt->GetActorLocation());
	}
	const int32 Steps = CountSteps(Mark);
	AddInfo(FString::Printf(TEXT("walked %.0f cm in 6 s, %d steps"), Walked, Steps));
	TestTrue(TEXT("it walked several strides"), Walked > 4.f * Tuning.GruntStepCm);
	TestTrue(TEXT("one step for each stride of ground walked"), FMath::Abs(Steps - Walked / Tuning.GruntStepCm) <= 1.5f);

	// Frozen while it walks: no steps.
	float Waited = 0.f;
	while (Waited < 20.f && Grunt->GetMotion().Velocity.Size2D() < 150.f)
	{
		World.Run(GruntAITestStep);
		Waited += GruntAITestStep;
	}
	World.Time().PressClapper();
	const int32 Frozen = Audio.GetAsked().Num();
	World.Run(2.f);
	TestEqual(TEXT("frozen, it makes no steps"), CountSteps(Frozen), 0);
	return true;
}

# strip.py <out.jpg> <cols> <img>... : tiles images into one JPG at most 960 wide, each labelled with its file name.
import sys
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw
out, cols, files = sys.argv[1], int(sys.argv[2]), sys.argv[3:]
w = 960 // cols
ims = []
for f in files:
    im = Image.open(f).convert('RGB')
    im = im.resize((w, int(im.height * w / im.width)))
    d = ImageDraw.Draw(im)
    name = f.replace('\\', '/').split('/')[-1].rsplit('.', 1)[0]
    d.rectangle([0, 0, 7 * len(name) + 6, 14], fill=(0, 0, 0))
    d.text((3, 1), name, fill=(255, 255, 255))
    ims.append(im)
h = ims[0].height
rows = (len(ims) + cols - 1) // cols
sheet = Image.new('RGB', (w * cols, h * rows))
for i, im in enumerate(ims):
    sheet.paste(im, ((i % cols) * w, (i // cols) * h))
sheet.save(out, quality=85)
print(out, sheet.size)
EOF

    with open(os.path.join(OUT, name + '.txt'), 'w', newline='\r\n') as f:
        f.write('\n'.join(lines) + '\n')
    print(name, len(lines), 'lines, ends', lines[-1])

def run_line(room, name):
    return f"# Run: farm.sh run c4 gruntai1 <logs> -Room tests/{room} -Seed 1 -Script {{P}}{BS}Script{BS}gruntai{BS}{name}.txt -FixedFps 60 -Silent"

def sweeps(ev, t0, t1, each=1.0):
    t, side = t0, 1
    while t + each <= t1:
        ev.append((round(t, 2), f"move 0 {side}")); side = -side; t += each
    ev.append((round(t, 2), "move 0 0"))

def shot(ev, t, enemy, name):
    ev.append((round(t - 0.03, 2), f"aim {enemy}")); ev.append((round(t, 2), f"shot {name}"))

def volley(ev, t, targets, per=3):
    n = 0
    for g in targets:
        for _ in range(per):
            ev.append((round(t, 2), f"aim {g}")); ev.append((round(t + 0.03, 2), "fire")); t += 0.22; n += 1
            if n % 6 == 0:
                ev.append((round(t + 0.05, 2), "reload")); t += 1.35
    return t

def walk(ev, t, legs):
    for x, y, secs in legs:
        ev.append((round(t, 2), f"lookat {x} {y} 152")); ev.append((round(t + 0.1, 2), "move 1 0")); t += 0.1 + secs
        ev.append((round(t, 2), "move 0 0")); t += 0.1
    return t

StateClock += DeltaSeconds;

	switch (State)
	{
	case ERusherState::Run:
		if (!CanSee(TargetActor, Tuning.RusherSightRange, RusherEyeHeight))
		{
			break;   // it waits where it is until it sees the player
		}
		TurnTowards(There, Tuning.RusherTurnRate, DeltaSeconds);
		if (FVector::Dist2D(Here, There) <= Tuning.RusherLungeRange)
		{
			Enter(ERusherState::Windup);
			UE_LOG(LogSupercut, Display, TEXT("RUSHER %d winds up, %.0f cm from the player"), GetIndex(), FVector::Dist2D(Here, There));
			break;
		}
		{
			bRanThisTick = true;
			FVector ToTarget = There - Here;
			ToTarget.Z = 0.f;
			FVector Next = Here + ToTarget.GetSafeNormal() * (Tuning.RusherRunSpeed * DeltaSeconds);
			const FVector2D Clamped = ClampToHome(Next);
			Next.X = Clamped.X;
			Next.Y = Clamped.Y;
			FHitResult Hit;
			SetActorLocation(Next, true, &Hit);
			if (Hit.bBlockingHit)
			{
				// Slide along what it ran into, so a crate corner does not stop it dead.
				FVector Slide = FVector::VectorPlaneProject(Next - GetActorLocation(), Hit.Normal);
				Slide.Z = 0.f;
				FVector SlideTo = GetActorLocation() + Slide;
				const FVector2D SlideClamped = ClampToHome(SlideTo);
				SlideTo.X = SlideClamped.X;
				SlideTo.Y = SlideClamped.Y;
				SetActorLocation(SlideTo, true);
			}
		}
		break;

	case ERusherState::Windup:
		TurnTowards(There, Tuning.RusherTurnRate, DeltaSeconds);
		if (StateClock >= Tuning.RusherWindup)
		{
			// The direction is fixed now. Where the player goes from here does not change it.
			FVector ToTarget = There - Here;
			ToTarget.Z = 0.f;
			LungeDirection = ToTarget.GetSafeNormal();
			SetActorRotation(FRotator(0.f, LungeDirection.Rotation().Yaw, 0.f));
			LungeLeft = Tuning.RusherLungeLength;
			Enter(ERusherState::Lunge);
			const float Seconds = FMath::Max(Gap, 0.f) / Tuning.RusherLungeSpeed;
			ShowClip(ESupercutClip::PunchCross, FMath::Min(RusherPunchReachSeconds / FMath::Max(Seconds, KINDA_SMALL_NUMBER), RusherPunchMaxRate));
		}
		break;
	case ERusherState::Recover:
		if (!IsClipPlaying(ESupercutClip::PunchCross))
		{
			ShowClip(ESupercutClip::Idle);   // after the punch has played out
		}
		break;
	}
}

	SetActorRotation(FRotator(0.f, Now.Yaw + Step, 0.f));
}

void ASupercutRoom::AddKillBox(const FBox& Box, const FString& Cause)
{
	KillBoxes.Add({ Box, Cause });
	if (Cause == TEXT("lava"))
	{
		USupercutAudio::Get(this).PlayNearBox(TEXT("lava_loop"), RootComponent, Box);   // the fire bed, heard only near the hazard's edge
	}
}

bool ASupercutRoom::TouchesKillBox(const FVector& At, float Radius, float HalfHeight) const
{
	const FVector Reach(Radius, Radius, HalfHeight);
	const FBox Body(At - Reach, At + Reach);
	return KillBoxes.ContainsByPredicate([&](const FKillBox& Kill) { return Kill.Box.Intersect(Body); });
}

	/** A game world playing one room. */
	struct FGruntAIWorld : FTestWorldWrapper
	{
		bool Start(const TCHAR* RoomName)
		{
			if (!CreateTestWorld(EWorldType::Game))
			{
				return false;
			}
			GetTestWorld()->GetWorldSettings()->DefaultGameMode = AGameModeBase::StaticClass();
			if (!BeginPlayInTestWorld())
			{
				return false;
			}
			Runner().Begin({ RoomName }, 1);
			return Runner().GetHero() && Runner().GetRoom();
		}

		void Run(float Seconds)
		{
			const int32 Ticks = FMath::RoundToInt(Seconds / GruntAITestStep);
			for (int32 Tick = 0; Tick < Ticks; ++Tick)
			{
				TickTestWorld(GruntAITestStep);

void ASupercutGrunt::PickSpot(const FSupercutWalkGrid& Grid, const AActor* TargetActor)
{
	const FSupercutTuning& Tuning = FSupercutTuning::Get();
	DecideWait = GruntDecideSeconds * (1.f + Random.FRand());
	BlockedClock = 0.f;
	const FVector Here = GetActorLocation();
	const FVector There = TargetActor->GetActorLocation();
	// Standing on an edge square (it was placed near a wall or a ledge): it plans from the nearest walkable one.
	int32 From = Grid.IndexAt(Here);
	if (!Grid.IsWalk(From))
	{
		From = Grid.NearestWalk(Here, GruntRecoverRings);
		if (From == INDEX_NONE)
		{
			return;   // nowhere safe in reach: it holds its place
		}
	}
	TArray<float> Walk;
	Grid.WalkDistances(From, GruntSpotSearchCm, Walk);

	// Where the other Grunts are going, or stand.
	TArray<FVector> Taken;
	for (TActorIterator<ASupercutGrunt> It(GetWorld()); It; ++It)
	{
		if (*It != this && !It->IsDying())
		{
			Taken.Add(It->bHasSpot ? It->Spot : It->GetActorLocation());
		}
	}

	// Every square it can walk to, scored without traces: 0 in the middle of the range band, 1 at its ends, more beyond;
	// a long walk and another Grunt's spot cost more; a little of its own random so two Grunts do not think alike.
	const float Middle = 0.5f * (Tuning.GruntMinRange + Tuning.GruntMaxRange);
	const float HalfBand = FMath::Max(1.f, 0.5f * (Tuning.GruntMaxRange - Tuning.GruntMinRange));
	struct FChoice
	{
		float Score;
		int32 Index;
	};
	TArray<FChoice> Choices;
	for (int32 Cell = 0; Cell < Walk.Num(); ++Cell)
	{
		if (Walk[Cell] < 0.f)
		{
			continue;
		}
		const FVector Floor = Grid.FloorAt(Cell);
		const float Off = FMath::Abs(float(FVector::Dist2D(Floor, There)) - Middle) / HalfBand;
		float Score = Off + 3.f * FMath::Max(0.f, Off - 1.f) + Walk[Cell] * GruntWalkCost + GruntJitter * Random.FRand();

			}
		}
		Choices.Add({ Score, Cell });
	}
	if (Choices.Num() == 0)
	{
		return;
	}
	Choices.Sort([](const FChoice& A, const FChoice& B) { return A.Score < B.Score || (A.Score == B.Score && A.Index < B.Index); });

	FCollisionQueryParams Params(SCENE_QUERY_STAT(SupercutGruntSpot), false, this);
	Params.AddIgnoredActor(TargetActor);

		return FVector2D(Point.X, Point.Y);
	}
	return FVector2D(FMath::Clamp(Point.X, Home.Min.X, Home.Max.X), FMath::Clamp(Point.Y, Home.Min.Y, Home.Max.Y));

bool FSupercutWalkGrid::CanWalkLine(const FVector& From, const FVector& To) const
{
	int32 Last = IndexAt(From);
	if (!IsWalk(Last))
	{
		return false;
	}
	const float Length = FVector::Dist2D(From, To);
	const int32 Steps = FMath::Max(1, FMath::CeilToInt(Length / (Settings.CellSize * WalkGridLineStep)));
	for (int32 Step = 1; Step <= Steps; ++Step)
	{
		const int32 Here = IndexAt(FMath::Lerp(From, To, float(Step) / Steps));
		if (Here != Last)
		{
			if (!Joined(Last, Here))
			{
				return false;
			}
			Last = Here;
		}
	}
	return true;
}

int32 FSupercutWalkGrid::NearestWalk(const FVector& Point, int32 Rings) const
{
	const int32 CX = FMath::FloorToInt((Point.X - Origin.X) / Settings.CellSize);
	const int32 CY = FMath::FloorToInt((Point.Y - Origin.Y) / Settings.CellSize);
	int32 Best = INDEX_NONE;
	double BestDistance = TNumericLimits<double>::Max();
	for (int32 Ring = 0; Ring <= Rings && Best == INDEX_NONE; ++Ring)
	{
		for (int32 Y = CY - Ring; Y <= CY + Ring; ++Y)
		{
			for (int32 X = CX - Ring; X <= CX + Ring; ++X)
			{
				if (FMath::Max(FMath::Abs(X - CX), FMath::Abs(Y - CY)) != Ring)
				{
					continue;   // only the ring itself
				}
				const int32 Index = IndexOf(X, Y);
				if (IsWalk(Index))
				{
					const double Distance = FVector::DistSquared2D(FloorAt(Index), Point);
					if (Distance < BestDistance)
					{
						BestDistance = Distance;
						Best = Index;
					}
				}
			}
		}
	}
	return Best;
}

FVector ASupercutGrunt::WantVelocity(const FSupercutWalkGrid& Grid)
{
	const FSupercutTuning& Tuning = FSupercutTuning::Get();
	const FVector Here = GetActorLocation();
	FVector Want = FVector::ZeroVector;
	while (PathAt < Path.Num() - 1 && FVector::Dist2D(Here, Path[PathAt]) < GruntArriveCm)
	{
		++PathAt;   // close enough to this corner: on to the next, so it rounds the corner instead of stopping on it
	}
	if (PathAt < Path.Num())
	{
		float Left = FVector::Dist2D(Here, Path[PathAt]);
		for (int32 Leg = PathAt + 1; Leg < Path.Num(); ++Leg)

			Left += FVector::Dist2D(Path[Leg - 1], Path[Leg]);

		if (Left < GruntThereCm)
		{
			PathAt = Path.Num();   // there
		}
		else
		{
			// As fast as it can go and still stop on the goal.
			const float Speed = FMath::Min(Tuning.GruntMoveSpeed, FMath::Sqrt(2.f * Tuning.GruntBrake * Left));
			Want = (Path[PathAt] - Here).GetSafeNormal2D() * Speed;
		}
	}
	// Give way: away from any other live enemy that is too near, more the nearer it is.
	if (Tuning.GruntGiveWay > 0.f)
	{
		for (TActorIterator<ASupercutEnemy> It(GetWorld()); It; ++It)

			if (*It == this || It->IsDying())

				continue;

			if (Apart < Tuning.GruntGiveWay && Apart > KINDA_SMALL_NUMBER)
			{
				Want += (Here - It->GetActorLocation()).GetSafeNormal2D() * (Tuning.GruntMoveSpeed * (1.f - Apart / Tuning.GruntGiveWay));
			}
		}
	}
	Want.Z = 0.f;
	return Want.GetClampedToMaxSize(Tuning.GruntMoveSpeed);
}

}

void FSupercutWalkGrid::Build(UWorld* World, const FSettings& InSettings, TFunctionRef<bool(const FVector& BodyCentre)> IsHazard)
{
	check(World && InSettings.Bounds.IsValid && InSettings.CellSize > 0.f);
	Settings = InSettings;
	const FBox& Bounds = Settings.Bounds;
	const float Cell = Settings.CellSize;
	Origin = FVector2D(Bounds.Min.X, Bounds.Min.Y);
	SizeX = FMath::Max(1, FMath::CeilToInt((Bounds.Max.X - Bounds.Min.X) / Cell));
	SizeY = FMath::Max(1, FMath::CeilToInt((Bounds.Max.Y - Bounds.Min.Y) / Cell));
	Cells.Init(ECell::None, SizeX * SizeY);
	Floors.Init(0.f, SizeX * SizeY);

	FCollisionQueryParams Params(SCENE_QUERY_STAT(SupercutWalkGrid), false);
	const FCollisionResponseParams Solids = WalkGridSolids();
	const FCollisionShape Body = FCollisionShape::MakeCapsule(Settings.Radius + WalkGridMargin, Settings.HalfHeight - 1.f);
	const float Top = Bounds.Max.Z + 50.f;
	const float Bottom = FMath::Max(Bounds.Min.Z, Settings.LowestFloor) - 10.f;

	for (int32 Y = 0; Y < SizeY; ++Y)
	{
		for (int32 X = 0; X < SizeX; ++X)
		{
			const int32 Index = IndexOf(X, Y);
			const FVector Middle = FloorAt(Index);

```
const FSupercutWalkGrid* USupercutNav::GetGrid()
{
	ASupercutRoom* Room = USupercutRun::Get(this).GetRoom();
	if (!Room)
	{
		return nullptr;
	}
	if (BuiltFor.Get() == Room && Grid.IsValid())
	{
		return Grid.Get();
	}

	// The room's solid parts, as the hall measures them (SupercutHall.cpp).
	const FSupercutTuning& Tuning = FSupercutTuning::Get();
	FSupercutWalkGrid::FSettings Settings;
	TInlineComponentArray<UPrimitiveComponent*> Parts(Room);
	for (const UPrimitiveComponent* Part : Parts)
	{
		if (Part->IsCollisionEnabled())
		{
			Settings.Bounds += Part->Bounds.GetBox();
		}
	}
	checkf(Settings.Bounds.IsValid, TEXT("USupercutNav: room %s has no solid parts"), *Room->GetRoomName());
	Settings.CellSize = Tuning.GruntCellSize;
	Settings.StepHeight = Tuning.GruntStepHeight;
	Settings.LowestFloor = Room->GetFallHeight();
	// A blade's bar lets bodies through while it turns and kills only the player, so the floor under the whole circle it sweeps
	// counts as a hazard: nobody walks into a turning blade.
	TArray<FBox> Sweeps;
	for (TActorIterator<ASupercutBlade> It(GetWorld()); It; ++It)
	{
		const FVector Bar = It->GetBarSize();
		const float Reach = Bar.Y * 0.5f;
		Sweeps.Add(FBox(FVector(-Bar.X * 0.5f, -Reach, -Reach), FVector(Bar.X * 0.5f, Reach, Reach)).TransformBy(It->GetActorTransform()));
	}
	Grid = MakeShared<FSupercutWalkGrid>();
	Grid->Build(GetWorld(), Settings, [&](const FVector& Centre)
	{
		const FVector Reach(Settings.Radius, Settings.Radius, Settings.HalfHeight);
		const FBox Body(Centre - Reach, Centre + Reach);
		return Room->TouchesKillBox(Centre, Settings.Radius, Settings.HalfHeight) || Sweeps.ContainsByPredicate([&](const FBox& Sweep) { return Sweep.Intersect(Body); });
	});
	BuiltFor = Room;
	UE_LOG(LogSupercut, Display, TEXT("NAV room %s grid %d x %d, walk %d, edge %d, blocked %d, hazard %d"), *Room->GetRoomName(), Grid->GetSizeX(), Grid->GetSizeY(),
		Grid->CountCells(FSupercutWalkGrid::ECell::Walk), Grid->CountCells(FSupercutWalkGrid::ECell::Edge), Grid->CountCells(FSupercutWalkGrid::ECell::Blocked),
		Grid->CountCells(FSupercutWalkGrid::ECell::Hazard));
	return Grid.Get();
}

Result:

```
* long enough. The whole room is its area; the home rectangle of its room line is kept for the record and binds nothing.
 *
 * How it moves: its speed builds and falls away (GruntAccel, GruntBrake), it steers round other enemies, and every step
 * is checked against the grid, so it never walks off a ledge, into a hazard or into a wall. It faces the player while
 * it sees them and its way of walking otherwise, turning at GruntTurnRate.
 *
 * Between shots it either strafes a step to the side or ducks (its capsule shrinks to GruntCrouchHalfHeight, so a shot
 * over it misses); for the windup it stops and stands. With no grid (a test world with no room) it holds its place.
 *
 * It writes Motion every frame it runs.
 */
UCLASS()
class ASupercutGrunt : public ASupercutEnemy
{
	GENERATED_BODY()

public:
	ASupercutGrunt();

	/** Call before BeginPlay. Home is recorded (GetHome) and binds nothing: the room is its area. */
	void Setup(int32 InIndex, const FBox2D& InHome);

	virtual const TCHAR* GetKindName() const override { return TEXT("GRUNT"); }

	FVector GetMuzzleLocation() const;

	/** The firing spot it is going to or fights from, once it has one. */
	bool HasSpot() const { return bHasSpot; }
	FVector GetSpot() const { return Spot; }

protected:
	virtual int32 GetStartHealth() const override;
	virtual void BuildBody() override;
	virtual void TickCombat(float DeltaSeconds, AActor* TargetActor) override;
	virtual void OnDying() override;
	virtual ESupercutClip GetRestClip() const override { return ESupercutClip::PistolIdle; }

private:
	enum class EPause : uint8
	{
		Stand,    // the wait between shots spent standing
		Strafe,   // a step to the side
		Duck,     // ducked down
	};

	void Fire(AActor* TargetActor);
	/** Chooses a firing spot and the path to it. */
	void PickSpot(const FSupercutWalkGrid& Grid, const AActor* TargetActor);

	const FSupercutTuning& Tuning = FSupercutTuning::Get();

	const FVector There = TargetActor->GetActorLocation();

	const bool bSees = CanSee(TargetActor, Tuning.GruntSightRange, GetEyeHeight());
	if (bSees)

		bAwake = true;
		UnseenClock = 0.f;
	}
	else
	{
		UnseenClock += DeltaSeconds;
	}

	// Fire on a steady clock. The clock waits at the start of the windup while the player is out of sight.
	const float WindupStart = Tuning.GruntFireInterval - Tuning.GruntWindup;
	const float ClockBefore = FireClock;
	FireClock += DeltaSeconds;
	if (!bSees)
	{
		FireClock = FMath::Min(FireClock, WindupStart);
	}
	if (ClockBefore <= WindupStart && FireClock > WindupStart)
	{
		USupercutAudio::Get(this).PlayAt(TEXT("grunt_windup"), GetMuzzleLocation());
	}

def write(name, header, ev):
    ev = sorted(ev, key=lambda e: e[0])
    lines = list(header) + [f"{t:.2f} {c}" for t, c in ev]
    with open(os.path.join(OUT, name + '.txt'), 'w', newline='\r\n') as f:
        f.write('\n'.join(lines) + '\n')

def sweeps(ev, t0, t1, each=1.0):
    t, side = t0, 1
    while t + each <= t1:
        ev.append((round(t, 2), f"move 0 {side}")); side = -side; t += each

**Sun 15 Nov 19:27:48 · Tool call: Bash** (Stage the fix blob only and commit it)

```
S="C:/Users/USER/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/ce66ae306241b5fa/2fcdcb15-f32c-467c-9766-b689126bd7db/scratchpad"; cd /d/UE/wt/gruntai1 && test -z "$(git diff --cached --name-only)" && B=$(git hash-object -w --path=Source/Supercut/SupercutGrunt.cpp "$S/fix/SupercutGrunt.cpp") && git update-index --cacheinfo 100644,$B,Source/Supercut/SupercutGrunt.cpp && git diff --cached --stat && cat > "$S/fix/msg.txt" <<'EOF'
SUPERCUT gruntai1: two Grunts never pick one firing spot

Crowding was only a score cost, and the close-in pick (no square in reach sees the
player) took the square nearest the player with no crowd check at all. In main's gen3
gen/s1/d06 (4 Grunts) the ones that could not see the player all walked to that square:
Supercut.GruntAI.MinutesOfFighting... counted 503 samples with two on one spot, on
5c55eff and on the stack 3446c2b alike.

Now a square within GruntSpotApartCm (100 cm, more than two Grunt radii) of another
Grunt's spot, or of where one stands, is never a choice, whichever way the spot is
picked. The test is unchanged.

bool ASupercutEnemy::CanStandAt(const FVector& Point) const
{
	const FSupercutWalkGrid* Grid = USupercutNav::Get(this).GetGrid();
	if (!Grid)
	{
		return true;
	}
	const int32 To = Grid->IndexAt(Point);
	if (To == INDEX_NONE || Grid->GetCell(To) == FSupercutWalkGrid::ECell::None)
	{
		return false;
	}
	const float Feet = GetActorLocation().Z - Capsule->GetUnscaledCapsuleHalfHeight() - 0.5f;
	return FMath::Abs(Grid->FloorAt(To).Z - Feet) <= FSupercutTuning::Get().GruntStepHeight
		&& !USupercutNav::Get(this).TouchesHazard(FVector(Point.X, Point.Y, GetActorLocation().Z), Capsule->GetScaledCapsuleRadius(), Capsule->GetScaledCapsuleHalfHeight());
}

FVector2D ASupercutEnemy::ShoveTarget(const FVector& Point) const
{
	// Walls, bodies and kill boxes stop a shove already (TickShove); the grid stops it at a ledge.
	const FVector Kept = CanStandAt(Point) ? Point : GetActorLocation();
	return FVector2D(Kept.X, Kept.Y);
}

void ASupercutEnemy::TickShake()
{
	if (USupercutTime::Get(this).IsFrozen())
	{
		return;   // the figure hangs where the freeze caught it
	}
	const FSupercutTuning& Tuning = FSupercutTuning::Get();
	ShakeLeft = FMath::Max(0.f, ShakeLeft - GetWorld()->GetDeltaSeconds());
	const float Size = Tuning.HitShakeCm * ShakeLeft / FMath::Max(Tuning.HitShakeSeconds, ShakeLeft);   // safe if F5 set it to 0
	Figure->SetRelativeLocation(FigureHome + ShakeRandom.GetUnitVector() * (Size * ShakeRandom.FRand()));
}

{
	const FSupercutTuning& Tuning = FSupercutTuning::Get();
	const FVector Here = GetActorLocation();
	const FVector There = TargetActor->GetActorLocation();

	// Can it see the player? A line from its head to the player's middle, stopped by walls and cover.
	const bool bSees = CanSee(TargetActor, Tuning.GruntSightRange, GetEyeHeight());
	if (bSees)
	{
		bAwake = true;
		UnseenClock = 0.f;
	}
	else
	{
		UnseenClock += DeltaSeconds;
	}

	const float WindupStart = Tuning.GruntFireInterval - Tuning.GruntWindup;
	const float ClockBefore = FireClock;

bool FSupercutWalkGrid::ArcClear(UWorld* World, int32 From, int32 To, TFunctionRef<bool(const FVector& BodyCentre)> IsHazard) const
{
	FVector Velocity;
	float Seconds = 0.f;
	JumpArc(FloorAt(From), FloorAt(To), Velocity, Seconds);
	FCollisionQueryParams Params(SCENE_QUERY_STAT(SupercutWalkGridArc), false);
	const FCollisionShape Body = FCollisionShape::MakeCapsule(Settings.Radius, Settings.HalfHeight);
	const FVector Start = FloorAt(From) + FVector(0.f, 0.f, Settings.HalfHeight + WalkGridArcLift);
	FVector Last = Start;
	for (int32 Piece = 1; Piece <= WalkGridArcSamples; ++Piece)
	{
		const float T = Seconds * Piece / WalkGridArcSamples;
		const FVector Point = Start + Velocity * T - FVector(0.f, 0.f, 0.5f * Settings.Gravity * T * T);
		if (World->SweepTestByChannel(Last, Point, FQuat::Identity, ECC_Pawn, Body, Params, WalkGridSolids()) || IsHazard(Point))
		{
			return false;
		}
		Last = Point;
	}
	return true;
}

bool FSupercutWalkGrid::HasJump(int32 From, int32 To) const
{
	if (From == INDEX_NONE || From >= Cells.Num())
	{
		return false;
	}
	for (int32 Jump = JumpFirst[From]; Jump < JumpFirst[From + 1]; ++Jump)
	{
		if (JumpTo[Jump] == To)
		{
			return true;
		}
	}
	return false;
}

int32 FSupercutWalkGrid::IndexAt(const FVector& Point) const
{
	return IndexOf(FMath::FloorToInt((Point.X - Origin.X) / Settings.CellSize), FMath::FloorToInt((Point.Y - Origin.Y) / Settings.CellSize));

	// The jumps, square by square in order, each square's ways in the same order.
	JumpFirst.Init(0, Cells.Num() + 1);
	JumpTo.Reset();
	for (int32 Index = 0; Index < Cells.Num(); ++Index)
	{
		JumpFirst[Index] = JumpTo.Num();
		if (Cells[Index] != ECell::Walk)
		{
			continue;
		}
		const int32 X = Index % SizeX;
		const int32 Y = Index / SizeX;
		for (const int32* Way : WalkGridWays)
		{
			const float Stride = Cell * ((Way[0] != 0 && Way[1] != 0) ? UE_SQRT_2 : 1.f);
			bool bGap = false;
			for (int32 Far = 1; Far * Stride <= Settings.JumpReach; ++Far)
			{
				const int32 To = IndexOf(X + Way[0] * Far, Y + Way[1] * Far);
				if (To == INDEX_NONE)
				{
					break;
				}
				if (Cells[To] == ECell::None || Cells[To] == ECell::Hazard)
				{
					bGap = true;
					continue;
				}
				if (Cells[To] != ECell::Walk)
				{
					continue;   // an edge or a ledge's foot: on over it
				}
				// The first walkable square this way ends the look. A jump only where walking does not do.
				const float Rise = Floors[To] - Floors[Index];
				if (Far > 1 && (bGap || FMath::Abs(Rise) > Settings.StepHeight) && Rise <= Settings.JumpRise && Rise >= -Settings.DropHeight
					&& ArcClear(World, Index, To, IsHazard))
				{
					JumpTo.Add(To);
				}
				break;
			}
		}
	}
	JumpFirst[Cells.Num()] = JumpTo.Num();
}

void FSupercutWalkGrid::JumpArc(const FVector& FromFloor, const FVector& ToFloor, FVector& OutVelocity, float& OutSeconds) const
{
	const float Peak = FMath::Max(FromFloor.Z, ToFloor.Z) + Settings.JumpApex;
	const float Up = FMath::Sqrt(2.f * (Peak - FromFloor.Z) / Settings.Gravity);
	const float Down = FMath::Sqrt(2.f * (Peak - ToFloor.Z) / Settings.Gravity);
	OutSeconds = Up + Down;
	OutVelocity = FVector((ToFloor.X - FromFloor.X) / OutSeconds, (ToFloor.Y - FromFloor.Y) / OutSeconds, Settings.Gravity * Up);
}

bool ASupercutGrunt::HasFloor() const
{
	// The body a little smaller than the capsule, swept down by a step: any solid under any part of it holds it up.
	FCollisionQueryParams Params(SCENE_QUERY_STAT(SupercutGruntFloor), false, this);
	Params.AddIgnoredComponents(Capsule->GetMoveIgnoreComponents());
	FCollisionResponseParams Solids(Capsule->GetCollisionResponseToChannels());
	Solids.CollisionResponse.SetResponse(ECC_Pawn, ECR_Ignore);
	const FVector Here = GetActorLocation();
	return GetWorld()->SweepTestByChannel(Here, Here - FVector(0.f, 0.f, FSupercutTuning::Get().GruntStepHeight + 5.f), FQuat::Identity, Capsule->GetCollisionObjectType(),
		Capsule->GetCollisionShape(-GruntSweepSkin), Params, Solids);
}

void ASupercutGrunt::StartAir(const FVector& Launch, float Gravity)
{
	bAir = true;
	AirFrom = GetActorLocation();
	AirVelocity = Launch;
	AirGravity = Gravity;
	AirClock = 0.f;
	Velocity = FVector::ZeroVector;
	Motion.bInAir = true;
	Motion.AirSeconds = 0.f;
}

void ASupercutGrunt::TickAir(float DeltaSeconds)
{
	AirClock += DeltaSeconds;
	const FVector Here = GetActorLocation();
	const FVector Now = AirVelocity - FVector(0.f, 0.f, AirGravity * AirClock);
	FVector There = AirFrom + AirVelocity * AirClock - FVector(0.f, 0.f, 0.5f * AirGravity * AirClock * AirClock);

	// Bodies do not stop it (it passes over or by them); walls, floors and ceilings do. A dead one's capsule no longer
	// collides, so the sweep is its own.
	FCollisionQueryParams Params(SCENE_QUERY_STAT(SupercutGruntAir), false, this);
	Params.AddIgnoredComponents(Capsule->GetMoveIgnoreComponents());
	FCollisionResponseParams Solids(Capsule->GetCollisionResponseToChannels());
	Solids.CollisionResponse.SetResponse(ECC_Pawn, ECR_Ignore);
	FHitResult Hit;
	bool bLands = false;
	if (GetWorld()->SweepSingleByChannel(Hit, Here, There, FQuat::Identity, Capsule->GetCollisionObjectType(), Capsule->GetCollisionShape(-GruntSweepSkin), Params, Solids))
	{
		There = Hit.bStartPenetrating ? Here : Hit.Location;
		if (Now.Z <= 0.f && (Hit.bStartPenetrating || Hit.ImpactNormal.Z >= GruntLandNormalZ))
		{
			bLands = true;
		}
		else
		{
			// A wall or a ceiling: the arc starts again from here, with what of its velocity runs along the surface.
			AirFrom = There;
			AirVelocity = FVector::VectorPlaneProject(Now, Hit.ImpactNormal);
			AirClock = 0.f;
		}
	}
	SetActorLocation(There);

	const ASupercutRoom* Room = USupercutRun::Get(this).GetRoom();
	const float Half = Capsule->GetUnscaledCapsuleHalfHeight();

IMPLEMENT_SIMPLE_AUTOMATION_TEST(FSupercutEncoreTest, "Supercut.Upgrades.EncoreReturnsAChargeForAHungKillOncePerFreeze", RunTestFlags)
bool FSupercutEncoreTest::RunTest(const FString& Parameters)
{
	FRunTestWorld World;
	if (!TestTrue(TEXT("test world starts"), World.Start()))
	{
		return false;
	}
	World.Run().Begin({ PlainRoom }, 1);
	World.Run().Grant(TEXT("encore"));
	USupercutTime& Time = World.Time();
	ASupercutCharacter* Hero = World.Hero();
	// Three Grunts fanned out in front, each one hit from dead.
	ASupercutGrunt* Left = World.SpawnTarget(1500.f, -30.f);
	ASupercutGrunt* Ahead = World.SpawnTarget(1500.f, 0.f);
	ASupercutGrunt* Right = World.SpawnTarget(1500.f, 30.f);
	World.Tick(0.05f);
	for (ASupercutGrunt* Grunt : { Left, Ahead, Right })
	{
		Grunt->TakeHit(2, FVector::ZeroVector);
	}
	World.SpendCharge();
	World.SpendCharge();
	TestEqual(TEXT("one charge left"), Time.GetCharges(), 1);

	// One freeze, two kills by hanging shots: one charge comes back, not two.
	Time.PressClapper();
	TestEqual(TEXT("the freeze took the last charge"), Time.GetCharges(), 0);
	Hero->SetActorRotation(FRotator(0.f, -30.f, 0.f));
	Hero->TryFire();
	World.Tick(0.3f);
	Hero->SetActorRotation(FRotator::ZeroRotator);
	Hero->TryFire();
	World.Tick(0.3f);
	TestEqual(TEXT("two shots hang"), World.Count<ASupercutShot>(), 2);
	Time.PressClapper();
	World.Tick(0.4f);
	TestTrue(TEXT("both Grunts are dead"), Left->IsDying() && Ahead->IsDying());
	TestEqual(TEXT("one charge came back"), Time.GetCharges(), 1);

	// A kill by a shot fired in rolling time gives nothing.
	Hero->SetActorRotation(FRotator(0.f, 30.f, 0.f));
	Hero->TryFire();
	World.Tick(0.4f);
	TestTrue(TEXT("the third Grunt is dead"), Right->IsDying());
	TestEqual(TEXT("a rolling kill returns nothing"), Time.GetCharges(), 1);
	return true;
}

```
void ASupercutGrunt::Tick(float DeltaSeconds)
{
	Super::Tick(DeltaSeconds);   // TickCombat, which may start a jump
	if (DeltaSeconds <= 0.f || !USupercutNav::Get(this).GetGrid())
	{
		return;   // frozen or held it hangs where it is; a bare test world has no floor to fall to
	}
	if (!bAir && !IsDying() && !HasFloor())
	{
		StartAir(FVector(Velocity.X, Velocity.Y, 0.f), FSupercutTuning::Get().GruntGravity);   // nothing under it: it falls
		UE_LOG(LogSupercut, Display, TEXT("GRUNT %d falls at %s"), GetIndex(), *GetActorLocation().ToCompactString());
	}
	if (bAir)
	{
		TickAir(DeltaSeconds);
	}
}

void ASupercutGrunt::Setup(int32 InIndex, const FBox2D& InHome)
{
	SetPlace(InIndex, InHome);
	// Stagger the first shots and the first sidestep so three Grunts do not act as one.
	FireClock = -0.45f * InIndex;
	StrafeSign = (InIndex % 2 == 0) ? 1.f : -1.f;
}

# farm step: runs one of the project's own Tools scripts in the mirror <Root>\Farm\<Name> and leaves its logs in
# <Root>\Farm\_out\<Name>\<Step>. Exit code: the Tools script's exit code.
# The project's package.cmd, package_shipping.cmd, run_tests.ps1 and run_demo.ps1 name c4's D:\UE\UE_5.9 and
# D:\UE\Builds. Each run writes a copy of the script beside it as Tools\farm_<file> with those paths mapped to this
# PC (engine <Root>\UE_5.9, builds <Root>\Farm\_builds\<Name>), and runs the copy. The next mirror deletes the copy
# (it is not on c4). Any other D:\ left in a copy stops the step.
param(
    [Parameter(Mandatory)][string]$Root,
    [Parameter(Mandatory)][string]$Name,
    [Parameter(Mandatory)][ValidateSet('build', 'test', 'package', 'package-shipping', 'run')][string]$Step,
    [string]$ArgsFile = ''   # one argument per line, passed on to the Tools script
)
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$proj = "$Root\Farm\$Name"
$engine = "$Root\UE_5.9"
$builds = "$Root\Farm\_builds\$Name"
$out = "$Root\Farm\_out\$Name\$Step"
if (-not (Test-Path "$proj\Supercut.uproject")) { Write-Output "FARM no project at $proj (mirror first)"; exit 10 }
if (-not (Test-Path "$engine\Engine\Build\Build.version")) { Write-Output "FARM no engine at $engine"; exit 11 }
if (Test-Path $out) { Remove-Item $out -Recurse -Force }
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force $out, $builds | Out-Null
$extra = @()
if ($ArgsFile) { $extra = @(Get-Content $ArgsFile | Where-Object { $_ -ne '' } | ForEach-Object { $_.Replace('{P}', $proj).Replace('{B}', $builds).Replace('{O}', $out) }) }

$latin1 = [Text.Encoding]::GetEncoding(28591)
function Map([string]$file) {
    $t = [IO.File]::ReadAllText("$proj\Tools\$file", $latin1)
    $t = $t.Replace('D:\UE\UE_5.9', $engine).Replace('D:\UE\Builds', $builds).Replace('cd /d D:\UE', "cd /d $Root")
    # On c4 itself (Root D:\UE) the D:\ paths are the right ones, so the check is for the other PCs only.
    if ($Root -notlike 'D:*' -and $t -match '(?i)\bD:\\') { throw "FARM Tools\$file names a D:\ path the farm does not map: $($Matches[0]) ... fix farm\remote\step.ps1" }
    $dst = "$proj\Tools\farm_$file"
    [IO.File]::WriteAllText($dst, $t, $latin1)
    $dst
}
function Keep([string[]]$files) { foreach ($f in $files) { if (Test-Path $f) { Copy-Item $f $out -Recurse -Force } } }

$logs = "$proj\Saved\Logs"
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Continue'   # under Stop, PowerShell 5.1 turns a native program's stderr line into a terminating error
# The lock on c4 says whose

# Writes the gruntai scripts (CRLF) into the worktree's Script/gruntai folder.
import os
OUT = r'D:/UE/wt/gruntai1/Script/gruntai'
BS = chr(92)

def write(name, header, ev):
    ev = sorted(ev, key=lambda e: e[0])
    lines = list(header) + [f"{t:.2f} {c}" for t, c in ev]
    with open(os.path.join(OUT, name + '.txt'), 'w', newline='\r\n') as f:
        f.write('\n'.join(lines) + '\n')
    print(name, len(lines), 'lines, ends', lines[-1])

def run_line(room, name):
    return f"# Run: farm.sh run c4 gruntai1 <logs> -Room tests/{room} -Seed 1 -Script {{P}}{BS}Script{BS}gruntai{BS}{name}.txt -FixedFps 60 -Silent"

def sweeps(ev, t0, t1, each=1.0):
    t, side = t0, 1
    while t + each <= t1:
        ev.append((round(t, 2), f"move 0 {side}")); side = -side; t += each
    ev.append((round(t, 2), "move 0 0"))

def shot(ev, t, enemy, name):
    ev.append((round(t - 0.03, 2), f"aim {enemy}")); ev.append((round(t, 2), f"shot {name}"))

def volley(ev, t, targets, per=3):
    n = 0
    for g in targets:
        for _ in range(per):
            ev.append((round(t, 2), f"aim {g}")); ev.append((round(t + 0.03, 2), "fire")); t += 0.22; n += 1
            if n % 6 == 0:
                ev.append((round(t + 0.05, 2), "reload")); t += 1.35
    return t

def walk(ev, t, legs):
    for x, y, secs in legs:
        ev.append((round(t, 2), f"lookat {x} {y} 152")); ev.append((round(t + 0.1, 2), "move 1 0")); t += 0.1 + secs
        ev.append((round(t, 2), "move 0 0")); t += 0.1
    return t

1:#!/bin/bash
2:# farm.sh: build, test, package and run a SUPERCUT project copy on a farm PC, driven from c4. Details: ../FARM.md.
3:#
4:#   farm.sh mirror  <host> <name> <project folder on c4>     copy the project to <root>\Farm\<name> (changed files only)
5:#   farm.sh build   <host> <name> <log folder> [build.ps1 args, e.g. -Target Supercut -Jobs 8]
6:#   farm.sh test    <host> <name> <log folder> [run_tests.ps1 args, e.g. -Filter Supercut.Rooms]
7:#   farm.sh package <host> <name> <log folder>               Tools\package.cmd   -> <root>\Farm\_builds\<name>\Supercut59
8:#   farm.sh package-shipping <host> <name> <log folder>      Tools\package_shipping.cmd -> ...\_builds\<name>\Supercut59_ship
9:#   farm.sh run     <host> <name> <log folder> [run_demo.ps1 args]   {P} = the mirror folder there, e.g. -Script {P}\Script\main8.txt
10:#   farm.sh fetch   <host> <name> <remote path> <local folder>   path in the mirror, or builds/... or out/...
11:#   farm.sh status  <host>
12:#   farm.sh slots                                             who holds or waits for which PC right now
13:#
14:# Each step brings its logs back to <log folder>/<step>/ and exits with the remote step's exit code.

	TestNearlyEqual(TEXT("held on its last frame"), Grunt->GetFigure()->GetPosition(), DeathLength, 0.01f);
	TestTrue(TEXT("the body is still there"), IsValid(Grunt));
	return true;
}

# strip.py <out.jpg> <cols> <img>... : tiles images into one JPG at most 960 wide, each labelled with its file name.
import os
import sys
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw

out, cols, files = sys.argv[1], int(sys.argv[2]), sys.argv[3:]
w = 960 // cols
ims = []
for f in files:
    im = Image.open(f).convert('RGB')
    im = im.resize((w, int(im.height * w / im.width)))
    d = ImageDraw.Draw(im)
    name = os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(f))[0]
    d.rectangle([0, 0, 7 * len(name) + 6, 14], fill=(0, 0, 0))
    d.text((3, 1), name, fill=(255, 255, 255))
```

That test says outright that the Grunt walks on in the frame it fires (SupercutFigureTests.cpp:244-248). The test isn't mine and I may not loosen it, so `4ee26da` undoes the change. You and that lane decide; the fix is three lines in `TickCombat`.
- **The door lane's room end broke four of my scripts.** `eight`, `cover`, `ledge` and `eight_frames` reached `end` without `RUN wrapped`. Three causes, all fixed in the scripts, no game code:
  - A sideways approach catches on the door frame.
  - In `eight` and `cover` the door is moved flush against the far wall, 201 cm past the room file's gate.
  - A `goto` still walking when the room ends never arrives, so the script fails.
- **The `ledge` and `eight` deaths you asked about were scripts that no longer fit the Grunt, not intent.**
  - `eight` fired blind volleys that could never reach Grunt 3 behind a wall, so Grunt 3 shot the player.
  - In `ledge`, the stage Grunt now jumps down off the stage (Stage 2) and fires early. With main's 35 per hit, the player died before the clap.
  - Both are rewritten to wrap under both revolvers.
- **My mistakes along the way.** A quoting bug crashed one batch of runs. A test Tuning.txt also lingered in the farm copies (the mirror doesn't delete root files), so one run used the wrong numbers. I removed it from both farm PCs; the final runs log `TUNING no file`.
